minutes.headline: Water District took no budget vote; it reviewed PFAS pilot testing, the Mass Ave main project and the bylaw map.
minutes.summary: Commissioners discussed the PFAS pilot test (water hardness and brine waste concerns), the nearly finished water main project, and a new per-unit fee on the October 1 bill. Public discussion covered the water protection bylaw map and the aging 1939 pipe system and how replacement is funded. Prior minutes were accepted and the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Questions to the superintendent on the planning board's water protection bylaw vote and which map (2009 vs 2021) goes to town meeting; wants a final map and a clean copy of the bylaw.
Asked for a copy of the written draft bylaw; asked whether the new fee is per unit and where the money goes.
Asked how widespread the old failing pipe is, the age of the system, the life expectancy of the pipe, and how replacement is funded.

votes.motion: Motion to accept minutes of a further meeting (date unclear, heard as 28).

budget_items.what_was_said: A fee per unit appears on the October 1 bill. The actual budgeted amount will be lower than planned because the budget assumed a per-connection basis.
The fee will be reset once the final bond issue amount is known, and the bill will show it as a project line item.

budget_items.topic: Main project cost versus budget and contingency
budget_items.what_was_said: The project is expected to be at or under budget, possibly touching contingency slightly.
Handheld belt clip readers were priced too high; a hub reader at the Sunny Hill tank is being priced.
Pricing will be for a gas truck because diesel trucks cannot be bought in Massachusetts for the 2025 model.
The master plan replacement is costly and unfunded; a state revolving fund application was not approved and in-house work saves engineering and prevailing wage costs.

decisions.decision: Water district will still submit the grant application for PFAS work, with the proposal possibly modified; decision on master plan details held until more data arrives.
The district wants the 2009 protection map plus the Lancaster Road addition (possibly a new 2024 map) sent with the bylaw; the superintendent will provide the maps.

what_happened.line: The Water District took no budget vote; the minutes record no votes beyond accepting prior minutes and adjourning.
Commissioners decided to still submit the PFAS grant application, possibly modified, and held master plan details until more data arrives.
The Mass Ave water main project is expected to finish at or under budget, and a per-unit connection fee appears on the October 1 bill.
The district wants the 2009 protection map plus the Lancaster Road addition sent with the bylaw; the superintendent will provide the maps.
Replacing the aging pipe system under the master plan is unfunded; a state revolving fund application was not approved.

why_it_matters: Water customers will see a new per-unit project fee on the October 1 bill, and it is to be reset once the final bond amount is known.
Replacing old pipe is costly and has no identified funding source, so the cost could later reach water bills or require a vote.
Which protection map goes with the water bylaw is still being settled, and that bylaw is one Town Meeting voters may be asked to take up.
watch_next: The final bond issue amount, which will reset the project fee shown on the bill.
The final protection map and a clean copy of the draft bylaw, which the superintendent is to provide.
